name: factstore-core
doc: The Part II conventions: composition, supersession, merges, money, documents, domain time and provenance.

attributes.doc: The whole this entity is part of or belongs to: a line's order, a shipment line's shipment.
The earlier entity this one replaces in the world, e.g. a reissued invoice.
The surviving entity this duplicate stands for; follow it when reading.

True on an attribute's own entity when the business that owns the store allows that attribute to hold personal data, such as a contact's name. Written by the business's owner or a manager with their own credential, never by an agent.
System authoritative for an attribute, e.g. shopify; asserted on the attribute's own entity.
ISO 4217 code of the currency every amount on this entity is in, such as an order's or a purchase order's.
Document backing a transaction's facts, asserted on the transaction. The document's issue date says when the facts were known.
First day of the accounting period an entity belongs to.
First date on which this entity's facts hold in the world.
Last date on which this entity's facts hold in the world.
Actor a transaction was written for, when the writer acts for someone else.
How sure the writer is of a transaction's facts, from 0 to 1.
SHA-256 of a document's bytes, in hex.
Where a document's bytes can be fetched.

When a document was issued or sent: the date printed on it, as midnight where it was issued, or a message's timestamp. To read what was known on a date, take the facts whose evidence was issued by then.
